question: Could a correct fix have been written in this DSL?
method: constructive, not judgement: candidate fixes written in the DSL, validated, and run on all 20 counterexample scenarios

variants_tested.fix: raise OncomingGapExceeds 5.5->9.0 in branches B and D
variants_tested.note: no effect: those branches are never reached

variants_tested.fix: add OncomingGapExceeds guard to branch C, swept 5.5 to 15.0 (validator max)
add PathIsClear to branch C, 16/24/32 m
variants_tested.note: guard blocks, ego creeps in anyway

variants_tested.fix: PathIsClear guard + fallback Decelerate(v_mps=0.0) true stop

mechanism: The frozen baseline commits from branch C (node n_22), which tests only DistanceToStopLineBelow(0.0). That is true once PAST the line, so it commits unconditionally and preempts the gap-guarded branch D. The gap thresholds at n_10, n_16, n_26 are never reached.

OncomingGapExceeds excludes any oncoming vehicle below min_speed_for_ttc_mps = 0.5. Measured on CE003: a vehicle 9.4 m away travelling at 0.04 m/s is EXCLUDED, so the predicate reports TTC = 30.0 s (the cap) and OncomingGapExceeds(15.0) PASSES while a stopped car sits in the junction. The time-based yield predicate is structurally blind to a stationary obstacle.

PathIsClear can see it. But when the guard blocks the commit the program falls through to Decelerate(v_mps=1.0), so the ego CREEPS at ~1.07 m/s and drifts across the conflict-zone boundary. Entry is delayed 2 s, not prevented.
Once inside, branch A (InConflictZone -> CommitTurn) commits unconditionally, bypassing every guard.
finding: A fix satisfying all five contracts IS expressible: guard the committing branch geometrically and make the fallback a true stop. It resolves 20/20. It also completes 0/20 and enters the junction 0/20. Across the family of edits tested, no expressible program both satisfied the contracts and completed the manoeuvre.
implication: This is a mechanistic explanation for the refusal result rather than a separate observation. Refusal is not the model being lazy; on this vocabulary and this failure mode it is the only expressible fix that satisfies the contracts. 72% of apparent repairs converging on it is what the language admits.
caveat: A family of edits was tested, not an exhaustive search of the program space. The claim is that no fix was found among natural single- and double-edit repairs, not that none exists.
